data.description:
Dpaste preserves eight locally saved task-artifact bodies. The SND subset shares exact dataset IDs and a filter/count task with known shorteners. A 54-link evidence inventory grades SND, GBBC, HIO and task-metadata cases; name-only candidates are supplemental.

Dpaste provides an additional public source of task artifacts consistent with automated retrieval, temporary storage, URL indirection and format experiments. The strongest bridge is profile 22219, sndproof37579: its surviving SND pastes share the exact Airtable view, share and application IDs and a specific Design/Award of Excellence filter/count task with the independently published shortener corpus. This establishes shared task/workflow provenance. It does not establish a common author, a particular provider, or communication between agents.

The main evidence is eight locally saved paste bodies and a 54-link activity inventory (bundle file: AGENT_ACTIVITY_LINKS.md): 14 profiles with task/workflow or task-metadata evidence, and 40 known paste IDs. AGENT_ACTIVITY_LINKS.tsv (bundle file: AGENT_ACTIVITY_LINKS.tsv) distinguishes directly inspected content from account-level inference and metadata-only cases, and supplies each link's confidence, availability, archive references, exact source path/line/hash, and local evidence. These are not 54 confirmed agents or independently verified exact content matches. Generic name candidates and unrelated material are excluded from this main inventory.

The supplemental census (bundle file: SUPPLEMENTAL_ALL_RECOVERED_LINKS.tsv) reconciles all 147 identified candidate/task links from the scoped inventories and reviewed report: 104 profile URLs and 43 known paste URLs, including explicit weak/unrelated exclusions. The 94 original candidates (bundle file: CANDIDATE_PROFILES.tsv) comprise 8 strong-name, 68 medium-pattern and 18 weak-name heuristics, not verified identities. Ten report-only profiles (bundle file: ADDITIONAL_REPORT_PROFILES.tsv) supplement that table. Ordinary entries from the broader 1,995-profile dataset are omitted. The original public directory is represented by fourteen scoped task-metadata excerpts (bundle file: evidence/archive_captures/dpaste_public_directory.task_entries.excerpt.inert.txt) with source line positions and the original file hash; unrelated directory content is not included. See coverage reconciliation (bundle file: COVERAGE.json).

SND is the high-confidence task bridge. Four saved SND bodies preserve the dataset URL, a stored URL intermediary, a Microlink retrieval function, and the specific filter/count procedure. The offline task comparison (bundle file: evidence/cross_surface/SND_filter_comparison.txt) and the independent task-family extract (bundle file: evidence/cross_surface/known_swarm__snd_task_family_analysis.md.excerpt.inert.txt) preserve view viwb5v6acVmfP9fnd, share shrMLVqYbqJ5nOxel and application app90oaiea9w9Ifs0. The shortener-chain excerpt (bundle file: evidence/cross_surface/known_swarm__snd_shortener_chains.txt.excerpt.inert.txt) preserves the 26 May sndfilter43x chain and task. These are public dataset identifiers; authentication signatures and secure viewer tokens have been redacted. The saved SND profile lists 19 paste IDs, but only four SND bodies are locally preserved and inspected here. The remaining fifteen are account/task-family metadata inferences, not nineteen independently verified exact content matches. A historical HTTP 200 does not mean a body is included or remains accessible now.

NVS is weaker. The archived public directory preserves eight named nvsproof paste IDs, systematic task titles and grouped additional-item counts, plus an anonymous NVS title. The known NVS shortener rows (bundle file: evidence/cross_surface/known_swarm__nvs_popcat_wayback_listing_rows.jsonl.excerpt.inert.txt) target the New Zealand National Vegetation Survey API. Missing Dpaste bodies prevent an exact endpoint comparison. This is a moderate task-family inference for the campaign; name-only nvsagent profiles remain tentative individually. Opaque IDs hidden behind “and N more” cannot be reconstructed and are not invented.

GBBC has three preserved bodies across two accounts. All three identify the same Canada 2024 Looker report; one body, 7UCRCRNKX from profile 22118, explicitly selects Ontario, Alberta, Yukon Territory and Northwest Territories. The public wiki extract (bundle file: evidence/cross_surface/gbbc_cross_surface__fangfufu_dokuwiki_export.txt.excerpt.inert.txt) preserves that same four-jurisdiction task. This is a strong task match between that paste and the wiki, with the other two pastes linked by report identity. No direct bridge to known collusion infrastructure has been established. HIO profile 22421 preserves seven Nigeria/Medical School paste IDs, one saved body, and a seven-to-one public-profile change. The separate cleanup finding adds a six-program correlation, but this source entry does not depend on that claim and does not present the disappearance as confirmed deletion or malicious conduct.

The stat*, bccref*, helper and other generated-name batches are mostly tentative candidates. Some have task-labelled directory metadata; most lack bodies. Ordinary game-script/browser-extension cases and generic weak names are retained for completeness with excluded dispositions. Discovery of a profile is not proof of agent authorship. Signup times, capture times and historical live checks have different meanings and must not be treated as one event timeline.

The bundle centers on eight redacted inert paste bodies, relevant profile captures, scoped directory metadata and selected existing comparison-source excerpts. Original candidate CSVs and the historical report are supplements for source reconciliation. All substantive comparisons can be reviewed offline. All HTTP status fields are historical observations from the saved records; no new checks were performed. Original and transformed hashes are distinguished in MANIFEST.json (bundle file: MANIFEST.json), with INDEX.tsv (bundle file: INDEX.tsv) and validation (bundle file: VALIDATION.json).

Untapped source: Yes, qualified. Dpaste may hold more relevant archival directory records, surviving public task artifacts and cross-surface matches beyond this reviewed collection. This does not imply access to private pastes or that expired/missing bodies remain recoverable. The present inventory is complete only for the specified local sources, not the entire platform. Cyberattack: None; government: No for the Dpaste platform, although linked tasks include public-sector data; AI system/provider: Unknown. Strong task linkage is separate from provider attribution.

No network requests, new profile enumeration, archive fetch, credential reuse, browser rendering, archived program execution or form submission occurred. Code, HTML and original Markdown documents are supplied only as inert text. Sensitive authentication values, including public signed access-policy values and secure viewer tokens, are not bundled.
